newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Monday thanks to a large number of new share issues on the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract soared to 15.50 percent from 8.50 percent last Friday.
Total turnover on the six-contract market rose to 5.1 million lots from 2.6 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
There were three new A share issues and four new listings on Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges on Monday.
"The new share issues greatly increased fund demand on the repo market today, leading some big institutions to borrow heavily, pushing up the rates and the volume," said one trader.
The strong performance of the A share markets was another factor supporting the rates, traders said.
All state banks began to trade their state debt repurchase contracts on the local currency interbank trading on Monday in accordance with a Beijing decree, traders said.
"With state banks moving to the interbank market, the exchange-based repo trading will become slower in the mid-term," said one trader.
Traders said they expected the exchange-based repo rates to move at the current high level in the next few days due to a large number of forthcoming new A share issues.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Monday mainly due to the brisk A share markets, traders said. The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 109.79 yuan from 110.07 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 1.2 million lots from 830,995 lots.
Traders said they believed the spot contracts would move narrowly around the current level in the short term.
